source_caption:
To capture the wildly stunning, fiercely immersive visual landscape of the 1930s Mississippi Delta, cinematographer Autumn Durald Arkapaw made massive, groundbreaking cinematic history. By deciding to shoot the highly anticipated horror epic entirely on large format film, she officially became the very first female director of photography to ever shoot a movie using IMAX cameras. To fully achieve the film’s profoundly unique, deeply atmospheric look, Kodak even completely invented a brand new 65mm version of their iconic Ektachrome film stock specifically for the production. By fiercely pushing the boundaries of traditional physical media, Arkapaw masterfully proves that the most terrifying, visually intoxicating nightmares are still best captured on real, aggressively breathtaking celluloid.
⠀
Sinners (2025), directed by Ryan Coogler, starring Michael B. Jordan, Hailee Steinfeld, Jack O’Connell. Trying to completely abandon their deeply troubled, violently criminal pasts in Chicago, twin brothers return to their rigidly segregated Mississippi hometown to open a juke joint, only to quickly realize they have accidentally invited a profoundly ancient, highly terrifying supernatural evil to a wildly chaotic, completely inescapable fight for survival.

source_details.title: Sinners
source_details.synopsis: Sinners is a 2025 American horror film produced, written, and directed by Ryan Coogler. Set in 1932 in the Mississippi Delta, it stars Michael B. Jordan in dual roles as criminal twin brothers who return to their hometown in the Jim Crow South, where they are confronted by a supernatural evil. The film co-stars Hailee Steinfeld, Miles Caton (in his film debut), Jack O'Connell, Wunmi Mosaku, Jayme Lawson, Omar Benson Miller, and Delroy Lindo. Coogler began developing Sinners through his production company Proximity Media, with Jordan cast in the lead role. The project was announced in January 2024, and after a bidding war, Warner Bros. Pictures acquired distribution rights the following month
